entries.title: Old glasshouse misting schedule
entries.text: At the Aster Vale botanical conservatory, the north glasshouse misting cycle ran every 40 minutes during daylight. Staff recorded humidity after each cycle.

entries.title: Revised glasshouse misting schedule
entries.text: The north glasshouse misting cycle was changed to every 25 minutes during daylight. The humidity log is still checked after each spray cycle.

entries.title: Old ceramic kiln cooldown rule
entries.text: The blue-clay kiln at the fictional Brindle Works had to cool below 90 degrees before its door could be opened after a firing.

entries.title: Updated ceramic kiln cooldown rule
entries.text: After a safety review, the Brindle Works blue-clay kiln door may be opened only once its temperature is below 70 degrees following a firing.

entries.title: Old fog beacon reporting interval
entries.text: The Lumen Shoal fog beacon sent a condition report to the keeper station once every six hours, including during clear weather.

entries.title: New fog beacon reporting interval
entries.text: The Lumen Shoal beacon now reports its condition every two hours. Reports continue in clear weather so the keeper station can detect a failed radio.

entries.title: Earlier moon-moth survey route
entries.text: The moon-moth survey began at Fern Arch and followed the eastern footpath to the reed pond, where observers counted adults for twenty minutes.

entries.title: Current moon-moth survey route
entries.text: The moon-moth survey route was moved to the western boardwalk, starting at Slate Gate and ending at the reed pond. Counts remain twenty minutes long.

entries.title: Old archive duplicate retention
entries.text: The fictional Cloudberry Archive kept duplicate weather folios for 30 days before removing the extra copy from cold storage.

entries.title: Revised archive duplicate retention
entries.text: Duplicate weather folios at the Cloudberry Archive are retained for 90 days before the extra copy is removed from cold storage.

entries.title: Old tram night service frequency
entries.text: The imaginary Alderloop tram ran every 18 minutes after 9 pm on the northern circuit, with the same interval on weekdays and weekends.

entries.title: Updated tram night service frequency
entries.text: Since the timetable revision, the Alderloop northern circuit runs every 12 minutes after 9 pm, on both weekdays and weekends.

entries.title: Former seed vault inspection interval
entries.text: The Ember Vale seed vault was inspected once each month for condensation and seal damage; a paper checklist was filed after inspection.

entries.title: New seed vault inspection interval
entries.text: The Ember Vale seed vault inspection now happens every two weeks, checking condensation and seal damage on the same paper checklist.

entries.title: Old glider launch wind limit
entries.text: At the imaginary Kestrel Ridge, training gliders could launch when measured crosswind stayed under 14 knots for five minutes.

entries.title: Revised glider launch wind limit
entries.text: Training gliders at Kestrel Ridge now require crosswind below 10 knots for five continuous minutes before launch approval.

entries.title: Earlier bell tower calibration
entries.text: The Nine Bells tower clock was calibrated against the valley noon chime on the first day of each month.

entries.title: Latest bell tower calibration
entries.text: The Nine Bells tower clock is now calibrated against the valley noon chime every Monday, rather than monthly.

entries.title: Earlier cistern sampling frequency
entries.text: Before the 2025 change, the fictional Mossglass cistern was sampled for mineral content every ten days, with each vial marked by basin number.

entries.title: Current cistern sampling frequency
entries.text: From 2025 onward, Mossglass cistern mineral samples are collected every four days; technicians still mark each vial with its basin number.

entries.title: Earlier map paper storage temperature
entries.text: The imaginary Northglass map room stored survey paper at 19 degrees Celsius to reduce brittleness during winter.

entries.title: Current map paper storage temperature
entries.text: Since the 2024 conservation update, Northglass survey paper is stored at 17 degrees Celsius to limit brittleness year round.

entries.title: Earlier kite festival wind cutoff
entries.text: The made-up Saffron Plain kite festival paused launches when gusts exceeded 22 kilometres per hour.

entries.title: Current kite festival wind cutoff
entries.text: The Saffron Plain festival now pauses kite launches above 18 kilometres per hour of gust speed, a change recorded in 2025.

entries.title: Earlier fern greenhouse lighting duration
entries.text: The imaginary Silver Fern nursery illuminated its propagation bench for 11 hours each day during the 2021 growing season.

entries.title: Current fern greenhouse lighting duration
entries.text: The Silver Fern propagation bench has used a 13-hour daily light period since the 2023 growing season.

entries.title: Earlier island ferry boarding window
entries.text: At fictional Pebble Key, the morning ferry boarding gate closed five minutes before departure during the 2022 summer schedule.

entries.title: Current island ferry boarding window
entries.text: Under the 2024 schedule, Pebble Key morning ferry boarding closes eight minutes before departure to allow a final manifest check.

entries.title: Earlier comet chart publication day
entries.text: The fictional Tallow Observatory published its comet visibility chart on the 10th day of each month in 2023.

entries.title: Current comet chart publication day
entries.text: Since January 2026, Tallow Observatory publishes its monthly comet visibility chart on the 5th day of the month.

entries.title: Map legend uses a hollow diamond for springs
entries.text: In the fictional Northglass atlas, a hollow diamond marks a natural spring, while a filled diamond marks a seasonal seep. This symbol distinction applies to every regional sheet.

entries.title: Weavers tie a double loop for repair markers
entries.text: At the imaginary Loomwater guild, a repair marker is a double loop of blue thread; a single loop means the cloth is awaiting inspection.

entries.title: Fossil drawer labels put species before site
entries.text: Every Amber Shelf fossil drawer label lists the species name first and the excavation site second, separated by a slash.

entries.title: Nine Bells clappers are made from bronze
entries.text: The nine tower clappers at the fictional Nine Bells are cast from bronze. Their outer housings are cedar, but the striking pieces are bronze.

entries.title: Cloudmint tea uses water just below boiling
entries.text: For the imaginary Cloudmint tea recipe, steep one spoon of leaves in water at 92 degrees Celsius for three minutes; the water should not be at a rolling boil.

entries.title: Alderloop miniature rail uses a 32 millimetre gauge
entries.text: The Alderloop museum miniature railway has a track gauge of 32 millimetres, measured between the inside edges of its two rails.

entries.title: Blue shell specimens are stored in paper sleeves
entries.text: At the fictional Lumen Shoal natural history room, blue shell specimens go in acid-free paper sleeves, not glass jars, to prevent trapped moisture.

entries.title: Market lanterns use amber glass
entries.text: The imaginary Brindle night market uses amber glass in its wayfinding lanterns. The color makes the signs readable without confusing them with white workshop lights.

entries.title: Ember Vale seed packets encode the harvest year
entries.text: Every Ember Vale seed packet prints the four-digit harvest year after the plant variety name. The year is a label field, not a measure of seed age in storage.
